title: Templates and DocumentFragment
learningObjectives: Explain templates and documentfragment and use the browser API with appropriate lifecycle and privacy safeguards.

understand.concept: The template element stores inert DOM content in its content DocumentFragment. cloneNode(true) creates a copy of the template content. DocumentFragment lets code build a group of nodes off-document and append them together.
understand.whyItMatters: Templates separate markup structure from data. Building fragments before appending can reduce repeated document updates and makes repeated UI patterns easier to manage.
understand.analogy: A template is a reusable mould; a fragment is a prepared group of parts ready to be placed into the page.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser API support, permission, lifecycle, and security rules vary by platform.

explain.narrative: Each template clone receives a safe text title. The fragment is appended to the list as one grouped update.

examples.explanation: Each template clone receives a safe text title. The fragment is appended to the list as one grouped update.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the API; permission and secure-context features require a supported environment.

practise.guidedTask: Render three course cards from a template and a data array. Keep user-provided titles as text.
practise.independentTask: Build a small feature using the API. Include feature detection, permission or failure handling, cleanup, and an accessible alternative where relevant.
hints: Do not assume the API is available in every browser.
Request sensitive permissions only after explaining why.
Clean up observers, workers, and listeners when no longer needed.
